paragraph: The higher education ministry's 2023-2024 statistical yearbook counts [3,076 of the 31,503 graduates of academic year 2022/23 in STEM, 9.8 per cent](<https://mescti.gov.ao/media/uploads/ANUARIO_ESTATISTICO_2023_2024_5824af246e.pdf>). Economia & Mercado, reporting the ministry's yearbook, gave [about 11 per cent of 29,302 graduates for 2022/23](<https://economiaemercado.com/artigo/apenas-11-dos-novos-licenciados-em-angola-formam-se-em-areas-de-tecnologicas-e-de-engenharia>). Both figures are below 13 per cent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need STEM graduates at 13 per cent or more of tertiary graduates, in the latest figure for 2023 or later, from UNESCO's series.

In 2025, [STEM graduates were 9.75 per cent of tertiary graduates in Burundi](<https://databrowser.uis.unesco.org/>), by the tertiary graduates series of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The series gives no figure for the years just before. No source found says whether it is rising or falling. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 13 per cent of tertiary graduates or more has been found. Preparing would need STEM graduates at 13 per cent or more of tertiary graduates, in the latest figure for 2023 or later, from UNESCO's series.
